title: Trump floats 'Trump Ocean'
ticker: BREAKING: Trump floats renaming the Atlantic or Pacific "Trump Ocean" at Tennessee rally
Trump also jokes about a "Trump Strait" for the Strait of Hormuz
Lake Ontario renamed "Lake America" by executive order on Aug. 27
Canada's Carney: Canadians will keep the name Lake Ontario
No formal plan announced for renaming an ocean

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: First the Gulf of Mexico. Then Lake Ontario. Now, President Trump says he may have his eye on *an entire ocean*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: At a campaign rally in Tennessee on Saturday night, the president floated renaming the Atlantic or the Pacific. Among the names he suggested: *Trump Ocean*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Tonight, we look at what he said, how it fits into a growing list of name changes, and how America's neighbors have been responding.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Also tonight: why Canada's leaders say *Lake America* will never catch on north of the border.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: How Mexico, the White House press corps and even *your map app* got pulled into the fight.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: And the big question: could an ocean really be next?

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Our reporter has the story from Clarksville.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The president was in Clarksville, Tennessee on Saturday, headlining a midterm rally at the F and M Bank Arena.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Musician *Kid Rock* opened the event, and the crowd filled the arena well before the president took the stage.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He was there to campaign for Tennessee Republicans, including Senator Bill Hagerty and Marsha Blackburn, who is running for governor.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: For much of the speech, the president focused on familiar themes, touting new investment in Tennessee and urging supporters to turn out in November.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He also took aim at Iran, calling the country's leaders *crazy*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: But it was a riff about geography that grabbed the headlines.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Pointing to his earlier decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico, the president told the crowd that what the country still needs is an ocean.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He suggested the Atlantic or the Pacific could become the *Trump Ocean*, or, as another option, the Ocean of the Americas.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He also said he was not looking to rename the Mississippi River, telling the crowd that he *loves Mississippi*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The crowd cheered and laughed. Several outlets described the remarks as a joke, and the president did not say which ocean he preferred.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He announced *no formal plan*, and there is no indication of any executive order on the subject.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Still, the idea is not entirely new.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The president first raised the possibility of renaming an ocean back in August, at the White House.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: According to reporters in the room, he said, we have a Gulf, and we have a lake. Now *all we need is an ocean*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: At the time, he mentioned both the Atlantic and the Pacific, without settling on a name.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On Saturday, the president went further, putting his own name forward as one of the options.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Unlike a gulf or a lake, both oceans border *dozens of countries*, and none of them would be bound by an American renaming.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The ocean remark is only the latest entry on a growing list. Here's how we got here.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In January of last year, shortly after taking office, President Trump signed an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the *Gulf of America*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Mexico's government rejected the change, and the new name applies only to how the U.S. federal government refers to the gulf.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Then, on August twenty seventh of this year, in the middle of a trade fight with Canada, the president signed another order, this time renaming Lake Ontario as *Lake America*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The order directs federal agencies to use the new name on their maps, documents and databases, *effective immediately*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Lake Ontario sits on the border between the United States and Canada, and Canada is *not bound* by the order.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And at Saturday's rally, the president added one more idea, saying he might rename the Strait of Hormuz the *Trump Strait*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: And the *Gulf of America* change was not just a line on a map. It sparked real fights, at home and abroad.

scenes.name: Claudia Sheinbaum
scenes.quote: Why don't we call it Mexican America?

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum answered with a joke of her own, pointing to an old map and suggesting North America be called *Mexican America*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Mexico has continued to use the name Gulf of Mexico, and has asked Google not to apply the new name to waters beyond U.S. jurisdiction.

scenes.name: Associated Press
scenes.quote: Barred from Oval Office events after declining to use "Gulf of America".

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In Washington, the White House *barred* Associated Press journalists from some events, after the news agency said it would keep using the name Gulf of Mexico.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The AP took the dispute to court, arguing the ban violated press freedom.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The president also declared February ninth, two thousand twenty five, the first ever *Gulf of America Day*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The *Lake America* order in particular has drawn a sharp response north of the border.

scenes.name: Mark Carney
scenes.quote: The name is more than 400 years old, predating both the Confederation of Canada and the Declaration of Independence.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canadians will keep using the original name.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He pointed out that the name Lake Ontario comes from the Wendat language, and is more than *four hundred years* old, older than both Canadian Confederation and the U.S. Declaration of Independence.

scenes.name: Tim Houston
scenes.quote: Real foolishness now. It's Lake Ontario, buddy.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Nova Scotia Premier Tim Houston was more blunt. *Real foolishness* now, he wrote. It's Lake Ontario, buddy.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ontario Premier Doug Ford dismissed the move as a lot of *rhetoric*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He also put up a sign near Grimsby, on the lake's shore, reading Lake Ontario, *Now and Always*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The change has already shown up on the apps millions of people use every day.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: After the U.S. government updated its official place names database, Google Maps began showing *Lake America* to users in the United States.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Users in Canada still see Lake Ontario, and users elsewhere see both names. It is the same approach Google took with the *Gulf of America*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Reuters reported that Apple also changed the name on the web version of *Apple Maps* in early September.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Not every map company has followed. *MapQuest* has said it intends to keep the original name.

scenes.name: JB Pritzker
scenes.quote: Lake Michigan is now Lake Illinois.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Criticism has come from inside the United States as well.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker mocked the order by sarcastically declaring that Lake Michigan would now be called *Lake Illinois*, and joking that he would annex Green Bay.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: So could the Atlantic or the Pacific actually be next?

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: For now, the White House has not announced any formal step toward renaming an ocean.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Even if the president did sign an order, it would only change the name used by the U.S. federal government, as with the gulf and the lake.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Other countries along the Atlantic and Pacific coasts would be under *no obligation* to follow.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Whether the *Trump Ocean* remains a rally line or becomes the next executive order is a question the president has not yet answered.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: With the midterms just weeks away, the president is expected to keep up a busy schedule of rallies. Reporting from Clarksville, for KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: To recap tonight's top story.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: At a rally in Clarksville, Tennessee, President Trump floated renaming the Atlantic or the Pacific as the *Trump Ocean*, or the Ocean of the Americas.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: At the same rally, he also joked about renaming the Strait of Hormuz as the *Trump Strait*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The White House has given no timeline, and no sign of an executive order. For now, the *Trump Ocean* remains a rally line.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: But after a gulf and a lake, few are ruling anything out.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: He announced *no formal plan*. The remark follows his orders renaming the Gulf of Mexico and, in August, Lake Ontario, a move Canada's leaders have firmly rejected.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We'll keep following the story as it develops.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: That's all for tonight. This has been KOWEN News. Thanks for watching, and good night.
